ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, given point $A(1,0)$, the $x$-axis is rotated clockwise by $60^\circ$ about point $A$ to intersect the $y$-axis at point $B$, and then point $B$ is rotated clockwise by $90^\circ$ about point $A$ to obtain point $C$. If point $Q$ is a point in the Cartesian coordinate system, and it satisfies that the quadrilateral $ABCQ$ is a parallelogram, what are the coordinates of point $Q$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $Q(x, y)$, \\
since quadrilateral $ABCQ$ is a parallelogram, \\
therefore $AC$ and $BQ$ are the diagonals of the parallelogram, \\
the midpoint of $AC$ is $\left(\frac{2+\sqrt{3}}{2}, \frac{1}{2}\right)$, the midpoint of $BQ$ is $\left(\frac{x}{2}, \frac{y+\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$, \\
therefore $\frac{2+\sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{x}{2}$, $\frac{1}{2}=\frac{y+\sqrt{3}}{2}$, \\
therefore $x=2+\sqrt{3}$, $y=1-\sqrt{3}$, \\
therefore $Q(x, y)=\boxed{(2+\sqrt{3}, 1-\sqrt{3})}$;

Vector AB=B-A=(0-1,√3-0)=(-1,√3). Vector (x,y) rotated clockwise 90° becomes (y,-x), so after AB is rotated, AC=(√3,1) is obtained. Therefore C=A+AC=(1+√3,1). solver_metadata.cot_raw: 图像描述：图中有直角坐标系，O 在原点，A 位于 x 轴正方向上且标为 A，B 位于 y 轴正方向上；线段 AB 从 B 向右下连接到 A，线段 AC 从 A 向右上连接到 C，图中也显示 B、C 在同一条斜线上，符合由 AB 绕 A 顺时针旋转 90°得到 AC 的结构。推理：A=(1,0)，OA=1。由图和题意，三角形 AOB 在 O 处为直角，且 ∠OAB=60°，所以 OB=OA·tan60°=√3，因此 B=(0,√3)。向量 AB=B-A=(-1,√3)，绕 A 顺时针旋转 90°时，向量 (x,y) 变为 (y,-x)，所以 AC=(√3,1)，于是 C=A+AC=(1+√3,1)。若 ABCQ 为按顺序排列的平行四边形，则 Q=A+C-B。代入得 Q=(1,0)+(1+√3,1)-(0,√3)=(2+√3,1-√3)。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, given point $A(1,0)$, the $x$-axis is rotated clockwise by $60^\circ$ about point $A$ to intersect the $y$-axis at point $B$, and then point $B$ is rotated clockwise by $90^\circ$ about point $A$ to obtain point $C$. If point $Q$ is a point in the Cartesian coordinate system, and it satisfies that the quadrilateral $ABCQ$ is a parallelogram, what are the coordinates of point $Q$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $Q(x, y)$, \\
since quadrilateral $ABCQ$ is a parallelogram, \\
therefore $AC$ and $BQ$ are the diagonals of the parallelogram, \\
the midpoint of $AC$ is $\left(\frac{2+\sqrt{3}}{2}, \frac{1}{2}\right)$, the midpoint of $BQ$ is $\left(\frac{x}{2}, \frac{y+\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$, \\
therefore $\frac{2+\sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{x}{2}$, $\frac{1}{2}=\frac{y+\sqrt{3}}{2}$, \\
therefore $x=2+\sqrt{3}$, $y=1-\sqrt{3}$, \\
therefore $Q(x, y)=\boxed{(2+\sqrt{3}, 1-\sqrt{3})}$;
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure is a standard rectangular coordinate system, with the x-axis horizontal to the right, the y-axis vertical upward, and the origin is O. Point A is on the positive half-axis of the x-axis, marked at the position (1,0); point B is on the positive half-axis of the y-axis; the figure draws the oblique line segment from B to A, as well as the line segment from A to C, C is located to the upper right of A, and there is also a line segment between B and C slanting downward to the right.

Reasoning: According to the problem statement, the original x-axis is rotated clockwise 60° around A(1,0), obtaining a straight line passing through A, whose slope is -tan60°=-√3. Therefore the equation of this straight line is y=-√3(x-1). Let x=0, then y=√3 can be obtained, so B=(0,√3). Next, point B is rotated clockwise 90° around A to obtain C. Vector AB=B-A=(0-1,√3-0)=(-1,√3). Vector (x,y) rotated clockwise 90° becomes (y,-x), so after AB is rotated, AC=(√3,1) is obtained. Therefore C=A+AC=(1+√3,1). If quadrilateral ABCQ is a parallelogram, in the vertex order A-B-C-Q, AC and BQ are diagonals, and the midpoints of the two are the same, therefore A+C=B+Q, that is, Q=A+C-B. Substituting A=(1,0), C=(1+√3,1), B=(0,√3), obtain Q=(1,0)+(1+√3,1)-(0,√3)=(2+√3,1-√3).
